courses.title: Docker for Developers: Create and Manage Docker Containers
courses.why: The most current developer-focused Docker course on LinkedIn Learning (Shelley Benhoff): building, running and managing containers the way you will in the project.

courses.title: Kubernetes: Microservices
courses.why: A short, recent course (Kim Schlesinger, a certification exam developer) on deploying microservices to a cluster and service discovery: exactly the shape of this path's project.

courses.title: Learning Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
courses.why: You have deployed to AKS at The Dot Corp; this course (Richard Hooper, Azure MVP) turns that hands-on work into a certificate and fills in the parts of AKS you may not have touched.

portals.name: Kubernetes basics tutorial (official)
portals.what: The official interactive walkthrough: create a cluster, deploy, expose, scale and update an app.

portals.name: Killercoda CKAD practice
portals.what: Free browser-based Kubernetes clusters with CKAD-style tasks; the best way to practise kubectl without installing anything.

portals.name: Docker: build and share a containerized application (official)
portals.what: Containerise an app, persist data, use multi-container apps and Compose, with image-building best practices.

portals.name: roadmap.sh Kubernetes roadmap
portals.what: A topic map from pods to operators, useful as a checklist; the matching Docker roadmap is at roadmap.sh/docker.

portals.name: GeeksforGeeks: Kubernetes interview questions
portals.what: Common Kubernetes interview questions to answer out loud; the site also has a Docker interview questions page.

assessments.name: Microsoft Applied Skills: Deploy cloud-native apps using Azure Container Apps
assessments.format: Interactive hands-on lab assessment on Microsoft Learn (ACR, Container Apps, Azure Pipelines CI, scaling, revisions); 72 hours between lab launches
assessments.credential: Microsoft Applied Skills credential on your Microsoft Learn profile, shareable to LinkedIn
assessments.why: A free, practical container credential in the Azure ecosystem you already work in. (The AKS Applied Skill was retired in June 2024, so this is the container one to take.)

assessments.name: Kubernetes and Cloud Native Associate (KCNA)
assessments.credential: CNCF certificate and digital badge, valid for 2 years
assessments.why: The entry-level Kubernetes certification: concepts, not command-line speed. A good first step if CKAD feels too far.

assessments.name: Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD)
assessments.format: 2-hour online proctored, performance-based exam: real tasks on a command line running Kubernetes (v1.37)
assessments.credential: CNCF certificate and digital badge, valid for 2 years
assessments.why: The Kubernetes certification developers are asked about. Practise on Killercoda until the tasks feel routine before booking.
